THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Split Plate Pizza Snack Box

Four no-cook pizza snack boxes with turkey pepperoni, cubed cheese, crackers, and cucumber. About 220 calories and 15g protein per box.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME10 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~220 cal | ~15g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 3-4 servings turkey pepperoni (Hormel or Applegate — 3/4 to 1 serving per box)
  • 4 cheese sticks (1 per box, cubed) — Sargento Colby-Jack shown
  • 2 servings Triscuit Thin Crisps (1/2 serving per box)
  • 1 large cucumber (sliced or chopped, to fill each box)
  • Optional at-home side: marinara for dipping (skip in the packed box to avoid mess)

You want a kid snack box that tastes like pizza night without the mess, and lands at ~220 cal / 15g protein per box. Make 4 boxes once, feeds 2 kids across 2 snack rounds. No cook, no assembly-line — 10 min flat.

Method

  1. 1.SET UP. Line up 4 divided snack boxes (any brand with 3-4 compartments — the pastel Bento-style boxes shown work great).
  2. 2.TURKEY PEPPERONI. Add 3/4 to 1 serving of turkey pepperoni to one compartment of each box. Kid appetite determines the exact count — small kids get ~5-6 slices, bigger kids get the full serving.
  3. 3.CHEESE STICK CUBES. Cube 1 cheese stick per box (Sargento Colby-Jack shown — mozzarella, sharp cheddar, or Monterey Jack also work). Add cubes to the next compartment.
  4. 4.THIN CRISPS. Add 1/2 serving Triscuit Thin Crisps per box for the crackly pizza-crust texture. Any small savory cracker works if Triscuits aren't available.
  5. 5.CUCUMBER TO FILL. Slice or chop cucumber and pack it into the remaining space in each box. Fresh crunch balances the salty savory side.
  6. 6.LID + CHILL. Snap lids on, refrigerate until snack time. Serve cold. If serving at home, marinara on the side for dipping — keep it OUT of the packed box to avoid soggy crackers + messy cleanup.

Storage and reheating

Store: Refrigerate covered snack boxes.

Reheat: Don't — serve cold. That's the whole snack-box format.

Lasts: Best within 2 days. Cucumber softens + Triscuits start to soften from ambient moisture past that point.

Estimated nutrition

~220 cal | ~15g protein.

~220 cal / 15g protein per snack box, approximate. Component breakdown: 3/4 serving turkey pepperoni (~50 cal / 7g protein) + 1 cheese stick (~80 cal / 6g protein) + 1/2 serving Triscuit Thin Crisps (~65 cal / 1g protein) + cucumber (~20 cal / 1g protein — varies by fill amount). Total: ~215 cal / ~15g protein. Marked estimated because turkey pepperoni servings per kid vary from 3/4 to 1 full serving. Snack Box series treats macros as approximate — per-brand label lookup for exact publish-worthy nutrition.

Brands I use

Hormel
Turkey Pepperoni (5 oz bag — ~70 cal / 9g protein per 17-slice serving)
The macro spine of the snack box. Turkey pepperoni is ~half the calories of regular pork pepperoni + the same familiar pizza flavor. 3/4 to 1 serving per box = ~7g protein from the meat alone.
Applegate
Natural Uncured Turkey Pepperoni (5 oz — same macro profile, cleaner label if you're brand-conscious)
Cleaner-label alternative to Hormel. No nitrates/nitrites added, humanely raised. Similar ~70 cal / 9g protein per serving. Sub freely — the recipe is brand-flexible.
Sargento
Colby-Jack Cheese Sticks (12-pack — ~80 cal / 6g protein per stick)
Kid-familiar cheese in a stick format that cubes easily. 1 stick per box = 6g protein from the cheese layer alone. Cross-brand candidate: any string cheese or Bel Kaukauna singles.
Triscuit
Thin Crisps (7.1 oz box — Original variety; ~130 cal / 3g protein per 30-cracker serving)
The crunch layer. Wheat-based, thinner than classic Triscuits so kid mouths handle them better. 1/2 serving per box = ~65 cal / 15 crackers.
